messages:
maria: FYI I'm seeing a spike in p99/95 for model:open-alpha after yesterday's kernel selection change. Root looks like more KV decode stalls and allocator churn during batching bursts. Anyone else? :eyes:

aj: saw the alert. quick profile shows workspace compaction frequency increase and ~30% more small free ops. nvprof snippet: `GPU memcpy: 12.4ms -> 18.1ms` for decode loop.

devon: hmm. do we have per-request decode caps enabled on that canary? if not, big batches can saturate KV decode and fragment the slab.

maria: canary used new kernel routing + larger default batch size. per-request decode cap was still at 0 (legacy).

liam: my hypothesis: kernel swap changed latency distribution so routing pushes more long-seq requests into same queue. That increases KV prefill evictions and forces recycler to split slabs more often -> fragmentation.

nina: what about slotting KV into per-model, per-seq buckets (slotting) so we minimize cross-model fragmentation? we tried static slots in early prototype but never rolled out.

aj: slotting could help if we also route batches by predicted cache-hit affinity. i.e., don't mix large-decoder requests with short-chat on same worker. add a small routing heuristic: prefer worker with >=X cached prefixes for that model.

maria: sounds good. would it be a band-aid for the allocator? also need to consider per-request decode cap to avoid a single request monopolizing KV decode. example config snippet we could try: ```json
{"routing": {"prefer_cached_affinity": true, "affinity_threshold": 4}, "decode": {"per_request_kv_cap": 6}}
```

devon: +1. Also we should enable aggressive slab coalescing on recycler for that canary: `recycler.coalesce_threshold=2ms` reduced small-fragment count in my local sim.

liam: did we measure p99 impact in perf benchmarks? the earlier sim I ran: baseline p99 78ms -> after kernel change 112ms. With slotting + decode cap -> 86ms. Not perfect but big improvement.

maria: nice. can we add a short experiment plan: 1) enable per_request_kv_cap=6 on canary cluster A 2) enable prefer_cached_affinity routing 3) toggled recycler.coalesce_threshold -> collect p50/p95/p99 and KV hit-rate and free-op counts.

nina: I'll own the canary rollout. plan: 10% traffic today, 50% tomorrow if no regressions. add metrics: `kv_prefill_evictions`, `slab_frag_rate`, `decode_throttle_backpressure`, `p99_latency_ms`.

aj: small note: kernel selection logic also needs a fallback to older kernel when slab_frag_rate spikes > 0.15. We saw a sharp cliff where fragmentation causes repeated OOMs. fallback rule: if spike for 5m -> revert kernel for traffic on that worker pool.

maria: agreed. add automated rollback policy in rollout yaml. also please add a short tracing span around `kv:decode_loop` so we can correlate decode spikes to batch composition.

devon: I'll add the span and a microbench harness to replay the offending traces. can someone paste the exact trace id from the alert?

maria: trace id 0x9ab3c from the 02:14 alert. attaching sample log: ```
[02:14:21] worker-12 decode loop start seq=2048 model=open-alpha cache_hits=1 batch_size=16 workspace_free_ops=129
[02:14:21] worker-12 prefill evict slab=3 reason=low_free contiguous=0
[02:14:21] worker-12 decode stall 0.023s backpressure=true
```

liam: that log lines up with my local repro. recycler was splitting slab 3 into 4 pieces causing later allocations to fall back to slower path.

nina: rolling out now to 10% with slotting+cap+coalesce. will post metrics in ~15m. :rocket:

deploy-bot: deployment started: canary/slotting-cap-coalesce -> cluster canary-a (10%) by nina at 2365509970

aj: quick reminder: add telemetry to show per-worker `predicted_affinity` vs actual `cache_hit_rate` so we can tune `affinity_threshold`.

maria: thanks folks. if this smooths p99 we can bake slotting into the routing policy and maybe make per_request_kv_cap adaptive based on worker load.

deploy-bot: deployment succeeded: canary/slotting-cap-coalesce -> cluster canary-a (10%) at 2365510305

nina: initial numbers: p50 -2ms, p95 -8ms, p99 -18ms on canary vs baseline. slab_frag_rate down ~42%, kv_prefill_evictions down ~35%. :tada:

liam: promising. next steps: run a 2h soak at 50% and validate no secondary regressions (throughput, GPU utilization).

maria: tagging this thread for docs/ops so we capture config knobs for future incidents. :memo:
